To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Deep Convolutional Networks can classify mammographic masses with a high degree of accuracy, 2) Transfer learning is an efficient way to train a deep model for this task, 3) Data augmentation can be used to improve generalizability, 4) The network learns features that are interpretable and can be used to explain its predictions, and 5) Our method outperforms human performance on the DDSM data set.
we present the first study to classify breast masses in mammogram using deep convolutional neural networks, and achieve state-of-the art results on the DDS dataset.

1) deep convolutional neural networks can be successfully used to directly classify breast masses in mammography as benign or malignant using only the mass appearance; 2) transfer learning from ImageNet can be successfully used for this task, but requires careful pre-processing and extensive data augmentation to achieve state-of-the art results; 3) we achieve state-of-the- art results on the DDSSM dataset, outperforming human performance.

The main takeaway from our work is that
Convolutional Neural Network models are capable of learning features from mammograms directly, without relying on hand-crafted features or segmentation.
Convolutional Neural Network models trained on a large number of natural image datasets can be adapted and fine-tuned for medical image classification tasks with minimal additional training data.
deep learning models can be successfully applied to mammograms to achieve state-of-the art performance, without the need for complex pre-processing, segmentation or hand-crafted features.
